facts.title: GEM 训练：Meta 如何将 LLM 规模广告基础模型效率翻倍
facts.event_hint: Meta GEM recommendation-model training co-design doubles end-to-end MFU
facts.problem: GEM combines trillions of sparse embeddings, billions of dense parameters, jagged and asymmetric sequences, and precision-sensitive ad objectives. Standard LLM kernels and parallelism therefore leave GPU compute underused, create communication exposure across thousands of GPUs, and force costly activation recomputation or imbalance.
facts.mechanism: Meta co-designs recommendation-specific kernels (JFA, GDPA, BlockAttention), mixed MXFP8/BF16 precision, topology-aware 5D parallelism, SM-free collectives, memory/checkpointing, and sequence-length-aware load balancing. JFA consumes jagged tensors without padding; GDPA unifies asymmetric attention; BlockAttention reduces long-history work; 2D FSDP plus expert parallelism handles dense parameters while fully sharded 2D model parallelism handles sparse tables. Communication groups and volume are matched to NVLink, intra-zone RoCE, and cross-zone bandwidth tiers.

evidence.claim: GEM's end-to-end training efficiency doubled to 20–25% MFU while total training FLOPs grew 4x over 12 months.
Jagged Flash Attention v4 delivered 40–140% TFLOPS improvement over v2, contributing 18.5% relative local MFU gain and 12% QPS gain under production jagged distributions.
evidence.source_locator: Meta Engineering post, Jagged Sequence Flash Attention

evidence.claim: Optimized GDPA achieves 2x forward and 1.6x backward speedup over baseline, up to 3.5x forward speedup over FlashAttention 4 for short K/V production settings, and over 30% end-to-end throughput improvement across the full model.
evidence.value: 2x forward; 1.6x backward; up to 3.5x vs FA4; >30% E2E
evidence.source_locator: Meta Engineering post, Generalized Dot-Product Attention

evidence.claim: Sliding-window attention reduced long-sequence self-attention latency by up to 68%, while TLX block attention improved self-attention layer MFU by 30.6% over Triton block attention.
evidence.baseline: Full attention and Triton block attention
evidence.condition: GEM user-history self-attention with fixed 64-token blocks

evidence.claim: The 5D topology-aware parallelism maps dense and sparse communication to different tiers: intra-node NVLink for fast expert exchanges, smaller inter-node FSDP groups, and reduced cross-zone replica messages.
evidence.condition: Eight GPUs per host, within-zone RoCE, and oversubscribed cross-zone RoCE

facts.evaluation_context: This is an engineering report on Meta's GEM ads recommendation foundation model, trained at LLM scale on several thousand current-generation GPUs. It reports component-kernel and end-to-end MFU/QPS gains, and describes a three-tier network hierarchy; the excerpt does not provide a neutral external baseline or full cluster topology counts.
facts.limitations: The measurements are Meta-specific, use internal recommendation workloads and latest-generation GPUs, and combine many simultaneous optimizations; component gains should not be summed as independent end-to-end improvements. The 20–25% MFU is recommendation-model MFU, not an LLM training comparison, and quality/accuracy constraints are described qualitatively except for neutral normalized entropy in one attention result. Portability to other hardware, model architectures, or network hierarchies is not established (inference).
facts.project_relevance: For AI-infrastructure tracking, GEM demonstrates that end-to-end scaling depends on jointly mapping communication volume and group size to network tiers, not merely adding parallel dimensions. It is a useful reference for separating local-kernel, precision, network-overlap, memory, and load-balancing contributions when evaluating TPN-like scheduling or GPU-cluster changes (inference).
